## PostedLedgerProjection

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ui.Services.Services.Accounting.PostedLedgerProjection</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/Accounting/PostedLedgerProjection.cs:19](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/Accounting/PostedLedgerProjection.cs#L19).

Presentation projection for the posted-journal ledger surface — the governed book of record, scoped by ledger period. Lives here rather than in the desktop assembly on purpose: WPF cannot execute its tests off Windows (Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App has no Linux build), so the decisions worth testing — which period is the default subject, whether a missing summary is a notice or a failure, how a period reads to an operator — are kept in a net10.0 assembly where they run on any platform. The desktop view model is a thin shell over these functions, and mirrors the browser panel&#x27;s behaviour so the two lanes cannot disagree about the book.

| <code>public static PostedLedgerPnlProjection ProjectPnl(LedgerPeriodPnlSummaryDto summary, AccountingBasisKindDto basis, int availableBasisCount);</code> | [src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/Accounting/PostedLedgerProjection.cs:347](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/Accounting/PostedLedgerProjection.cs#L347) | Scopes a period&#x27;s P&amp;L to one accounting basis. The endpoint&#x27;s TotalRevenue and TotalExpenses are plain sums of the lines it returns, across every basis the period holds, so a GAAP trial balance sat beside a P&amp;L that added Primary and GAAP together. Summing the same lines filtered to one basis reproduces the endpoint&#x27;s figures exactly for a single-basis period and scopes them correctly for a mixed one. Net income is derived as revenue less expenses, the way the server derives its own realized figures, because the endpoint&#x27;s NetIncome is a period-level value that cannot be attributed to one basis. This is the desktop and browser workstations&#x27; shared definition of those figures: the two clients showing different revenue for the same period and basis is the conflation this exists to prevent. |

## ColorPalette

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ui.Services.Services.ColorPalette</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/ColorPalette.cs:17](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/ColorPalette.cs#L17).

Platform-agnostic color palette defining all ARGB color values used across desktop applications. Both platform BrushRegistry classes reference this shared source of truth for color definitions and state-to-color mapping logic. These are the runtime twins of src/Meridian.Wpf/Styles/ThemeTokens.xaml. Charting, QuantScript and the ScottPlot surfaces render from here rather than from the XAML resources, so a value that moves there must move here in the same change or the two identities split — which is exactly what happened when the desktop lane was restyled and this file was not. The static palette follows the institutional light card/data surfaces in Design System 4.3.0. ThemeServiceBase changes window theme state, not these immutable values; plot backgrounds and their ink therefore remain paired in either window mode. Every core value names its XAML twin.

## DesktopOperatorPreferenceSync

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ui.Services.Services.DesktopOperatorPreferenceSync</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/DesktopOperatorPreferences.cs:267](../../../../src/Meridian.Ui.Services/Services/DesktopOperatorPreferences.cs#L267).

Keeps the desktop shell&#x27;s theme, density and keyboard shortcut overrides in step with the operator&#x27;s host preferences, the same set the browser workstation syncs (OperatorPreferencesDto). On start, the values the host holds are applied. Theme and density are not saved back: the desktop does not persist its theme, so its startup theme is a default, not an operator choice. Desktop shortcut overrides (OperatorPreferenceValuesDto.DesktopKeyBindings) held by the host replace this desktop&#x27;s, including an empty set (every default). When the host has none yet, this desktop&#x27;s own overrides are saved up, so the first desktop to sync seeds them. When the operator changes the theme or density here, the latest host set is re-read and saved with only the appearance and density replaced; a shortcut change likewise replaces only the desktop shortcut overrides. Browser-only values (time zone, page descriptions, browser shortcut overrides, a spacious density) are kept. Notification choices and quiet hours (OperatorPreferenceValuesDto.Notifications) held by the host replace this desktop&#x27;s at start; a desktop change saves only that set. When the host cannot be read at start (no session, an older host, offline), the desktop stays local for the run and saves nothing. A failed save keeps the local change. The display time zone is applied to Meridian.Ui.Services.DisplayTimeZone, which desktop timestamps are formatted in; it is read at start and again whenever the desktop saves.
